title: Things the article says about your life that aren't in your words
meta: Inner Child Therapy · turn 41 (2026-10-10) · nothing on this page has been changed
intro: After the San Pedro line, I checked every sentence of the article that says something about your life (57 of them) against your guide and your messages in the records. 28 are backed by them. These are the rest that matter. Two aren't in your words at all, and the others say more than you did.

Each note quotes the sentence, says what your own words say, and gives my suggestion. Tell me which ones are true and I'll leave those. For the rest, my default is to bring them back to what your words say, then check Pangram again.
Rows are in the article's order. Nothing here has been changed yet.

rows.label: The Guide paragraph: your words, changed
rows.article: The Guide is the one people overlook the most.
notes: The sentence: "I left it out of my first version of this guide until Key pointed it out, and without an inner Guide, it's easy to go looking for one in a cult."

Your words (2026-09-27): "I overlooked this one in my original guide until Key pointed it out. And this is what leads people into cults if they don't have an inner guide." The Key part is yours. "It's easy to go looking for one in a cult" softens what you said and adds a reason (looking for a guide).
Suggestion: "...and without an inner Guide, that's what leads people into cults."

rows.label: My Journey P1: says more than you did
notes: The sentence: "But an old childhood wound could still hit and suddenly I was the same little kid again, even when the spiritual part of me felt completely free."

Your guide says people chase spiritual freedom to get above childhood trauma, and the trauma keeps running them from underneath, and "I was doing that as well until a few years ago, because I didn't know about the inner child." It doesn't say a wound would hit and you'd feel like the little kid again.
Is that true for you? If not: "I was doing that too until a few years ago, because I didn't know about the inner child."

rows.label: "this little me actually hurting": says more than you did
rows.article: Nobody leaves a baby starving on purpose.
notes: The sentence: "Then there was this little me actually hurting, and I could send some of the love I'd already found his way."

Your guide: "through direct experience I discovered he's really in there!", and to the reader, "you'll naturally offer him/her the love and freedom you've hopefully found". "Actually hurting", and that you sent him love, are added.
Is it true? If not, I'd keep only that you found out he's really in there.

rows.label: "It didn't for me": your third person made first
notes: The sentences: "It didn't for me." (ordinary life giving enough love and meaning) and "Conditional love felt radically insufficient, so I kept looking for something deeper."
Your guide says this about "somebody who feels that ordinary life and conditional love are radically insufficient", not about you, and it also says you were well-loved as a child.
Is it you? If not, I'd put it back to "for some people".

rows.label: "and later in loveyhuasca": adds an order
notes: Your guide lists the love that was already there: "from my parents, Buddhist teachings (which it turns out also include inner-child self-love!), and loveyhuasca." "Later" puts loveyhuasca after Buddhism, and your list doesn't give an order.
Suggestion: drop "later".

rows.label: The grown-up-me line: not in your words
rows.article: Sometimes I'd get past a protective part
notes: The sentences: "Sometimes I'd get past a protective part and reach the child, then get pulled so far into being him that there wasn't a grown-up me around anymore. The three adult jobs from the map don't work too well when the adult has vanished, so I started looking for a way to have an adult there before I could reliably be that adult myself."

I wrote the first one on 2026-09-16. Nothing of yours says it, and it's the line the San Pedro sentence was built on. Your guide has the idea as a phase of the method: "a bootstrap phase for people who can't yet occupy the adult role", and "Before you can reliably become the inner parent, you may need to experience, imagine, imitate, and practice one adult function with help."
Suggestion: unless it's true for you, say it the guide's way, about people who can't be the adult yet, not as your own story.

rows.label: "When I talk with folks like that": adds that you do
rows.article: When I talk with folks like that
notes: Your guide has these as questions for the reader to ask ("What does this identity give you, what does it cost, and whom does it serve?"). Your 2026-09-25 note is about the urge ("what's really essential is the fact that they are obeying an urge, so how is that sovereignty? it sounds more like slavery"), and that part is yours. That you talk with people like that came from my wording (its record says model-written, and you accepted it at the time), and a later record called it yours.
Is it true? If not: "With folks like that, I'd want to know...".

rows.label: "that hurt": not in your words
rows.article: And yeah, going back to the writer
notes: The sentence: "A lot of the time it's just "that hurt."" It's said about your own inner child's angry drafts. I added it on 2026-09-25, and your words stop at the pencil sentence.
Is it true of your drafts? If not, I'd make it general ("A lot of the time the draft just means "that hurt."").

rows.label: "I did this too": your Tyler lesson, reframed
notes: You said the Tyler story is "about how to voice your concerns about others' behaviors coming from concern about your own behaviors" (2026-09-27). The sentence makes it something your own inner child's drafts say, and the story that follows is Tyler speaking, not a draft of yours. The Tyler story itself is all backed by the chat you pasted.
Suggestion: make the line general too, as above.

headings: # Borrow the Adult Before You Can Be the Adult

rows.label: "I was, and baby me was still starving": says more than you did
rows.article: If you can tell your parts apart pretty easily
notes: The sentence says you were one of the meditators who are great at watching, and your inner child was still starving. Your guide says you were bypassing until a few years ago, and it has the starving baby, but about "you". The record called this line my "deliberate callback" and said you could veto it.
Is it true? If not, I'd cut "I was, and baby me was still starving."
